item.title: Anchored HLLD: A Riemann solver for a hypoelastic diffuse-interface model of compressible fluid-solid interaction
item.description: arXiv:2610.31958v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an HLLD Riemann solver for a multicomponent hypoelastic diffuse-interface model of compressible fluid-solid interaction, with no separately computed interface and a deviatoric stress advanced by an objective hypoelastic rate law outside conservation-law form. The difficulty specific to this model is that the stress evolution is nonconservative and, unlike the familiar volume-fraction terms of Kapila-type models, cannot be left outside the Riemann solve once the shear waves are resolved. The shear coefficient $\rho(G+\tau_{xx})$ sets the impedance of the resolved shear waves and so belongs to their eigenstructure. Anchored HLLD carries it inside the solve by evaluating the HLLD fan twice at each face, anchored in turn to each adjacent cell-centered state, with every cell advancing from the flux anchored to its own state. HLL, HLLC, and anchored HLLD form a three-tier hierarchy of increasing wave resolution in one framework. We prove local structural properties: consistency at the reconstruction order, exact species-mass conservation, and tangential-momentum and energy drift vanishing under refinement at the reconstruction's face-jump order on smooth fields, with one-dimensional tests illustrating these structural properties and demonstrating first-order drift convergence on discontinuous fields. Across one-dimensional tests and two-dimensional production simulations in the open-source solver MFC, anchored HLLD resolves both the material contact and the shear waves, HLLC the contact alone, and HLL neither sharply. Where refinement studies are shown, anchored HLLD converges toward exact or semi-analytic solutions. A three-dimensional shock-ellipsoid interaction demonstrates the solver with all six stress components active.
item.dc:creator: Yanjun Zhang, Tim Colonius

item.title: Coherent axion electrodynamics in OSIRIS: a counter-propagating axion-photon parametric instability
item.description: arXiv:2610.32091v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a coherent axion-electrodynamics extension of the OSIRIS particle-in-cell code and use it to identify and benchmark a parametric axion-photon instability supported by two equal counter-propagating electromagnetic pumps. The module evolves a cell-centered axion field together with a separately stored first-order electromagnetic response on the native staggered OSIRIS grid. Re-examining the previously proposed strictly co-linear branch shows that it is removed when the axion-Maxwell equations are reduced consistently. A closely related standing-wave geometry, however, supports a distinct Floquet instability. We derive the coupled Floquet problem for an equal-amplitude counter-propagating pump pair and obtain a reduced analytic growth rate and cutoff for the dominant long-wavelength envelope branch. For an axion mass-to-pump-frequency ratio of 0.06 and a per-beam vector-potential amplitude of 0.3, simulations at coupling strengths of 0.60, 0.80, and 1.00 reproduce both the growth-rate spectrum and the coupling-dependent instability boundary. The reduced theory predicts envelope-mode cutoffs of 8.44, 10.80, and 13.23, while OSIRIS finds exponential growth through modes 8, 10, and 13, respectively, with the next resolved modes stable. The electromagnetic diagnostics additionally resolve exponentially growing sidebands at twice the pump wavenumber, while the zero-wavenumber electric component exhibits no sustained growth, as expected for the unstable Floquet eigenvector. The agreement provides an end-to-end benchmark of the coherent axion-electromagnetic coupling and demonstrates that parametric growth of the axion field is present in a two-beam pump geometry.
item.dc:creator: Miles Radford, Pablo Bilbao, Thomas Grismayer, Luis Silva, Robert Bingham, Subir Sarkar, Gianluca Gregori

item.title: CoPiT: A conditional Position-induced Transformer for aerodynamic field prediction on unstructured meshes
item.description: arXiv:2610.32299v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-fidelity Reynolds-averaged Navier--Stokes (RANS) simulations remain a standard tool for aerodynamic analysis, yet each solve on an unstructured mesh is computationally expensive, making many-query tasks such as design exploration, optimization, and multi-condition evaluation costly. Neural operators provide mesh-flexible surrogates for mapping geometry and operating conditions to flow fields; however, in many existing architectures, global parameters such as the freestream state and design variables are concatenated with pointwise inputs, leaving their influence on intermediate features implicit. This paper proposes CoPiT, a \textbf{Co}nditional \textbf{P}osition-induced \textbf{T}ransformer that builds on the Position-induced Transformer (PiT) as its geometric backbone and injects a global condition vector through multi-stage feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM), thereby making parametric modulation explicit while preserving geometry-based attention weights. The model is evaluated on two-dimensional AirfRANS airfoil fields, including scarce-data and extrapolation regimes, and on three-dimensional BlendedNet++ blended-wing-body surfaces. On the AirfRANS full-data test set, CoPiT reduces surface and volume losses by approximately 54\% and 24\% relative to Transolver, respectively, and achieves the lowest overall normalized test MSE among the compared baselines on BlendedNet++. Matched ablations show that FiLM conditioning generally improves upon input concatenation, while the preferred placement is task-dependent. CoPiT thus provides a practical operator-learning surrogate for parametric aerodynamics on unstructured meshes.
item.dc:creator: Junfeng Chen, Yongchen Fan, Zhonghua Qiao, Kailiang Wu

item.title: Compression of turbulent flow data through an extended space-time correlation: certification against the modal energy budget
item.description: arXiv:2610.32427v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The fidelity of direct numerical simulation now outpaces the storage and data-movement capacity available for the resulting fields. We present an open, distributed, GPU-accelerated low-rank compression framework for large turbulent flow databases. We assess it using two direct numerical simulations of a controlled diffusion compressor cascade under laminar and turbulent inflow conditions. Compression is formulated using a correlation operator over space and time, which is two orders of magnitude larger than that of snapshot POD. Its dominant range is extracted with a randomized range finder based on communication-avoiding hierarchical QR. The compressed databases are evaluated through a hierarchy of increasingly strict diagnostics, from instantaneous reconstruction and second-order statistics to the modal turbulent kinetic energy budget and its nonlinear interscale transfer. The budget terms are far more sensitive to compression than fieldwise or one-point errors. They remain accurate at conservative compression and degrade sharply once the retained energy is relaxed. The near-wall dissipation and the interscale transfer degrade the most and set the admissible compression level. An aggressive reduction preserves every one-point statistic to within a few per cent while corrupting both by an order of magnitude more. The dissipation error is confined to the viscous sublayer and grows with the development of the boundary layer. It is carried by the high-order modes. For both inflows, the linear budget terms scale with the discarded energy to the power $0.8$ and the triadic transfer to a power above one.
item.dc:creator: Gustavo Lopes, Davide Lengani, Dan Henningson

item.title: QuantumBilliards.jl: An extensible, user friendly, high-performance Julia library for the large scale computation of spectra and eigenstates of quantum billiards and related problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.32605v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present QuantumBilliards.jl, an open-source Julia library providing a suite of numerical solvers for the two-dimensional interior Helmholtz eigenproblem with Dirichlet boundary conditions, a paradigmatic model in quantum chaos. The library implements conventional wavenumber-sweep techniques together with several accelerated eigensolvers: the Vergini--Saraceno scaling method, the expanded boundary integral method (EBIM), Beyn's contour-integral method, and the Compact Rational Krylov (CORK) method. It provides a common framework for constructing billiard geometries, exploiting discrete symmetries, computing eigenvalues and eigenstates, and treating smooth, cornered, and multiply connected domains. The library further includes reconstruction of eigenfunctions from boundary normal derivatives and the computation of Poincar\'e--Husimi (PH) phase-space representations. Available at: https://github.com/Quantum-Chaos-Julia/QuantumBilliards.jl.
item.dc:creator: Matic Orel, \v{C}rt Lozej

item.title: foap4: Adaptive mesh refinement with OpenACC/OpenMP, MPI, and p4est
item.description: arXiv:2605.07612v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: GPUs and other accelerators are increasingly used for scientific computing. We want to add GPU support to existing parallel adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) codes written in Fortran. To understand which changes are necessary to obtain good performance we have developed foap4, an AMR framework implemented in Fortran that uses OpenACC/OpenMP, MPI, and the p4est library. We discuss the design and implementation of the framework. Several benchmark problems are considered, in which Euler's equations of gas dynamics are solved using explicit time integration. These benchmarks are performed in both 2D and 3D, using static and adaptive meshes, for varying problem sizes on different hardware. Our results show that AMR simulations can be carried out efficiently on GPUs, even when using relatively small grid blocks of $8^3$ or $16^3$ cells. With NVIDIA's nvfortran compiler similar performance is obtained with OpenACC and OpenMP offloading. Initial results with the gfortran compiler and OpenACC demonstrate the portability of foap4.
item.dc:creator: Jannis Teunissen, H\'ector R. Olivares S\'anchez, Jesse Vos, Leon Oostrum, Johan Hidding, Victor Azizi, Yuhao Zhou, Hao Wu, Adrian Kelly, Olaf Willocx, Chun Xia, Rony Keppens, Oliver Porth

item.title: CodeJeNN: A simple C++ neural network generator for physics applications
item.description: arXiv:2607.02746v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Machine learning has shown promise for physics applications, but integrating Python-based libraries into high-performance C++ solvers can create performance bottlenecks. We present CodeJeNN, which addresses this gap by auto-generating self-contained C++ code from trained Keras models for inference. This eliminates external dependencies through inlined functions, allowing seamless integration into existing frameworks. We describe the Keras-to-C++ workflow, supported architectures, and limitations. CodeJeNN is demonstrated through inference benchmarks against Keras (eager and optimized) and a computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulation of a hydrogen-air mixing layer in which viscosity is modeled using a neural network, showing that the generated models integrate directly into a solver while remaining efficient and accurate.
item.dc:creator: Jay Arcities, Pavel Popov, Eric J Ching, Kamal Viswanath, Ryan F Johnson

item.title: Adding slow magnetoacoustic mode to the HLL-type multi-state approximate Riemann solution
item.description: arXiv:2609.17049v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Multi-state HLL-type approximate Riemann solutions of ideal magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) typically assume that the medium within the Riemann fan is incompressible, and thus the slow magnetoacoustic mode cannot be included in their space-time wave configurations for the intermediate states. We propose a new strategy to design multi-state HLL-type solutions, allowing for the medium within the Riemann fan to be compressible. In particular, for the complete seven-wave configuration of the MHD Riemann problem, we estimate the slow magnetoacoustic speeds and a longitudinal flow speed between the slow modes, whose compressibility is estimated based on the relations between fast, Alfv\'en, and slow speeds. Then, following the conservation laws and Rankine-Hugoniot jump relations across the fast, Alfv\'en, and slow waves, we calculate all the intermediate states within the Riemann fan. Moreover, we discuss the solutions when certain wave modes degenerate, ensuring well-posedness and smooth transitions between complete and degenerate wave configurations. Numerical simulations using a Finite Volume solver show that the proposed approximate Riemann solution is less diffusive than the classic HLLD scheme, particularly for slow mode waves. For example, in a 1D test case with a strong longitudinal magnetic field, the new scheme needs one order of magnitude fewer grid cells compared to the classic HLLD scheme to resolve all wave modes.
item.dc:creator: Fan Zhang, Stefaan Poedts, Andrea Lani

item.title: Stabilizing the parquet problem
item.description: arXiv:2606.04936v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We systematically analyze the stability of the iterative solution of the parquet equations by studying the spectrum of the Jacobian associated with the commonly used damped fixed-point iteration procedure. In this context, we provide an explicit criterion that determines when the physical fixed point of the parquet iteration becomes unstable. Importantly, we demonstrate that misleading convergence issues, observed in parquet calculations at intermediate-to-high interaction values, are not restricted to parameter regions where the two-particle irreducible vertex diverges, but can also arise in absence of vertex divergences. Hence, the misleading convergence issues of parquet-based algorithms are not directly caused by the crossings of two solutions of the (multivalued) Luttinger-Ward functional, that are associated with vertex divergences. Building on these insights, we apply the controlled stabilization strategy of Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 016502 (2026) to the challenging case of the parquet iteration. This strategy allows the convergence to the physical solution in the instability regimes. We apply this procedure to the zero-point model and the Hubbard model in the atomic limit, where we successfully stabilize the physical solution deep in the non-perturbative regime, even across multiple divergence lines. Further, we compare our stabilization strategy to alternative fixed-point solvers that can be used to solve the parquet problem.
item.dc:creator: Herbert E{\ss}l, Stefan Rohshap, Marcel Gievers, Markus Wallerberger, Alessandro Toschi, Anna Kauch

item.title: Temperature-Dependent Multiphysics Modeling of Additive Friction Stir Deposition Using Multi-Task Coupled Physics-Informed Neural Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.04082v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Additive friction stir deposition (AFSD) involves coupled thermal and material-flow fields governed by frictional heating, plastic deformation, and tool-imposed boundary conditions. High-fidelity finite-volume methods (FVMs) can resolve these fields but are computationally expensive, while constant-property approximations can distort the predicted thermo-mechanical response. This work develops a steady-state multi-task coupled physics-informed neural network (MCoPINN) to predict three-dimensional temperature and material-flow fields while reconstructing temperature-dependent thermal conductivity, density, and specific heat from sparse property measurements. A theoretical analysis decomposes prediction error into property reconstruction and neural field-solver contributions and characterizes the discrepancy associated with constant-property models. A controlled one-dimensional nonlinear-conduction study evaluates property reconstruction under sparse measurements. The framework is then evaluated for AFSD against a temperature-dependent FVM benchmark and experimental thermocouple measurements. MCoPINN reproduces the reference thermal and material-flow fields and reduces average temperature root-mean-square error from 50.13 K for the constant-property CoPINN to 30.28 K across four traverse speeds. MCoPINN requires approximately 8.5 hours of training per condition, compared with 52 hours for the FVM benchmark. These results demonstrate computationally efficient, physics-coupled prediction with temperature-dependent material properties.
item.dc:creator: Dhrubajyoti Gupta, Nikhil Gotawala, Raghav Gnanasambandam, Rohit Kannan, Jian Yu, Hang Z. Yu, Zhenyu James Kong

item.title: Solubility of poorly soluble species in bulk and nanopores from grand-canonical Wang-Landau sampling
item.description: arXiv:2610.16599v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Poorly soluble species can have mean populations below one in small systems such as nanopores. In this regime, the grand-potential minimum, which identifies the most probable particle number, differs from the ensemble-averaged solute loading. We use grand-canonical Wang-Landau sampling (GCWLS) to calculate the density of states $\Omega(N_\mathrm{A}, N_\mathrm{B})$ for a binary Lennard-Jones mixture of solute B in solvent A, both in bulk and in slit pores. One set of GCWLS simulations gives ensemble averages over a range of chemical potentials, whereas conventional grand-canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC) simulation requires a separate simulation at each state point. Independent GCMC simulations confirm the GCWLS ensemble averages. The solvent number distribution is nearly Gaussian, whereas the dilute solute distribution is skewed and Poisson-like. The most probable solute number therefore lies below the ensemble-averaged loading $\langle N_\mathrm{B}\rangle$ and is zero whenever $\langle N_\mathrm{B}\rangle<1$. Reading the solute loading from the grand-potential minimum underestimates it and can falsely indicate that no solute is present. Defining the oversolubility as $\mathcal{O}_\mathrm{B}=x_\mathrm{B}^{\mathrm{conf}}/x_\mathrm{B}^{\mathrm{bulk}}$, where $x_\mathrm{B}$ is the solute mole fraction, we find $\mathcal{O}_\mathrm{B}\approx12$ in a pore of 3.5 particle diameters width when both wall interactions are repulsive. Adding wall-solute attraction moderately raises it to $\approx13$, whereas wall-solvent attraction lowers it to $\approx3.4$. This comparison shows that the wall-solvent interaction controls most of the enhancement. As the pore widens, $\mathcal{O}_\mathrm{B}$ decreases toward unity. In bulk and in nanopores alike, the solubility of poorly soluble species should be obtained from ensemble averages rather than from grand-potential minima.
item.dc:creator: Russell Kajouri, Adyant Agrawal, Philipp St\"ark, Alexander Schlaich, Christian Holm

item.title: Residual-Based Adaptive Refinement in Hybrid Variational-Collocation PINNs for Singular Elliptic PDEs with Mixed Dirichlet-Neumann Boundary Conditions
item.description: arXiv:2610.26458v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Solutions of second-order elliptic PDE problems on nonconvex or cracked domains with mixed Dirichlet-Neumann conditions typically lie outside $H^2(\Omega)$. Near re-entrant corners, crack tips and points where the boundary condition changes type, the gradient grows like $r^{\lambda-1}$ with $\lambda<1$. We study residual-based adaptive refinement in hybrid variational-collocation PINNs. A multiscale Fourier-feature network is trained on a composite loss. The loss combines a variational residual tested against Legendre bubble functions, a strong-form collocation term and penalties for the Dirichlet and Neumann data. The variational term needs only first derivatives of the network, whereas the collocation term requires second derivatives and provides a residual that can be evaluated at any point. After each training stage, candidate points selected by this residual are added to the collocation set. The method is tested on five two dimensional benchmarks, namely a Mode~III crack, a cross-shaped domain with four re-entrant corners with unequal amplitude, a reaction-diffusion problem with four localized peaks, a monotone semilinear problem with a boundary layer and the Motz problem. Compared with uniform point insertion under the same collocation and iteration budget, residual-based refinement reduced the relative $L^2$ error by up to a factor of $32$, the relative $L^\infty$ error by up to a factor of $38$ and the relative $H^1$ semi-norm error by up to a factor of $15$.
item.dc:creator: Somnath Giri, Muslim Malik, Rishikesh Yadav
